coordinates.object_orientation: Long axis +Z, surviving basal end at z=0. Fig9 exterior/adapertural side faces front camera -Y, wing extends -X; aperture is opposite side (+Y), hidden photo-side depth conservative. Top +Z and side +X standard.

concept.reason: Actual complete readable diagnostic winged fossil photograph and same-specimen measured dimensions suffice.

primary_specimen: Weidemeyer2009 specimen268, Tafel14 Fig9, locality SM43
scope: Only specimen268 in Plate14 Fig9; genus-level original target. Retain aff.osiris uncertainty. Not PRI60021 or S.camachoi, no Eocene/10cm data mixed in.

scale.basis: Weidemeyer p192 table: specimen268 H44.0mm, B25.0mm, wing-inclusiveB42.0mm. Depth23mm is inferred working proportion, not measured.
scale.uncertainty: Adapertural photo shows exterior opposite aperture. Exact unseen interior/rim depth not measured; conserve surviving fossil outline rather than restore missing shell.

required_features: Recognizable high stepped conical spire above inflated body whorl, roughly four preserved whorls; retain observed worn top instead of extending a needle tip.
Broad attached labral wing, continuous with body shell. Strong posterior wing process curves up and reaches above penultimate whorl. It is not a loose fin.
Wing exterior margin is roughly straight; broad upper concavity joins the upper wing tip to body. Anterior process weak/blunt rather than a second equal long spike.
Body whorl has two principal keels, posterior stronger; coarser nodules on upper whorls, restrained fine spiral sculpture. Simplify microstriae rather than create50 expensive ridges.
Match only Fig9 silhouette and relative widths. Fig10/11 smaller specimens must not replace missing parts, Fig12/13 are different species, Fig15-17 different genus.
Short blunt basal end as preserved; no long unsupported siphonal tail. Unknown opposite-side aperture may be a conservative shallow recess, not elaborate restored anatomy.
